summary: The self_healing component is the learn-and-recover layer of the loop. ErrorLearner records each ErrorOccurrence, mines recurring ErrorPatterns, and recommends a RecoveryStrategy; the RecoveryTree classifies a FailureSignal into a FailureKind and dispatches a RecoveryDirective (retry, compress context, reload credentials, fallback); StateManager snapshots StateCheckpoints and restores them; HealthPredictor projects a HealthPrediction (Healthy/AtRisk/Degrading/FailureImminent) to act before failure. It turns the loop's ErrorRecovery branch from ad-hoc into a learning system that reshapes retry budget and state transitions.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed reading src/self_healing/ (mod ErrorLearner/StateManager/HealthPredictor, recovery_tree, executor) in the context of the full engine at a ~600k budget framing, where self_healing drives the ErrorRecovery state of the Planning->Executing->ErrorRecovery loop.

examples.title: Record every error occurrence
examples.intent: Log each failure with type, message, and context so patterns can emerge.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ErrorLearner.record ingests an ErrorOccurrence on every failure, building the memory the recovery decisions later draw on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the self-healing node to see the latest recorded ErrorOccurrences as a stack.
touch_interaction.visual: Each occurrence drops in as a red card tagged with its error_type and count.

examples.mini_scenario: A tool times out; ErrorLearner.record captures the occurrence with its context so a pattern can form across repeats.
examples.pitfall: Record with enough context to disambiguate; identical messages from different sites must not collapse into one pattern.

examples.title: Mine recurring error patterns
examples.intent: Detect that the same failure keeps happening.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Repeated ErrorOccurrences roll up into an ErrorPattern with a count, raising the priority of a durable fix over one-off retries.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread the node to fan out patterns ranked by frequency.
touch_interaction.visual: Patterns render as bars whose length grows with occurrence count; hot patterns glow.

examples.mini_scenario: The same DNS failure recurs five times; the ErrorPattern count climbs and the learner elevates it as a systemic issue.
examples.pitfall: Age out stale patterns; a long-resolved issue that keeps a high count skews future recommendations.

examples.title: Recommend a recovery strategy
examples.intent: Pick the recovery action most likely to work for this error type.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: recommend_recovery returns a RecoveryStrategy (retry/restart/fallback/restore) that the ErrorRecovery branch executes instead of blind retry.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap an error pattern to see its recommended RecoveryStrategy and past success rate.
touch_interaction.visual: The strategy chip shows an icon per action; its border thickness reflects historical success.

examples.mini_scenario: A context-overflow error matches a pattern whose learned strategy is compress-and-retry, so recommend_recovery returns that.
examples.pitfall: Prefer strategies with proven success rates; recommending an untested action for a critical error wastes the retry budget.

examples.title: Classify a failure into a FailureKind
examples.intent: Turn a raw error message into a routable FailureKind.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: classify maps the FailureSignal to a FailureKind (LlmUnreachable, RateLimited, ContextOverflow, ...), selecting which recovery branch the loop takes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a failure event to reveal its classified FailureKind badge.
touch_interaction.visual: Each kind has a distinct icon and color; ambiguous ones resolve to a gray Unknown tag.

examples.mini_scenario: An error 'timed out connecting' classifies as LlmUnreachable, not a generic ToolTimeout, thanks to the deliberate ordering.
examples.pitfall: Respect the classification order; checking generic timeout before connect phrases mis-routes network failures.

examples.title: Dispatch a RecoveryDirective
examples.intent: Execute the concrete recovery the RecoveryTree resolved.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RecoveryTree.resolve returns a RecoveryDirective (Action, CompressContext, ReloadCredentials) that the loop applies before re-attempting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the recovery node back into the executor to apply the directive.
touch_interaction.visual: The directive travels the edge as a labeled token (RETRY / COMPRESS / RELOAD) that lands on the target stage.

examples.mini_scenario: A ContextOverflow yields a CompressContext directive with a target_tokens, so the loop compresses history then retries.
examples.pitfall: Apply the directive before retrying, not after; retrying an overflowing context without compressing repeats the failure.

examples.title: Compress context to recover from overflow
examples.intent: Shrink the conversation to fit the model window and continue.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The CompressContext directive reduces token usage to roughly target_tokens, freeing budget so the loop can iterate again.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the context node to preview the compression target on a token gauge.
touch_interaction.visual: The context bar squeezes from red-over-limit down to green-under-target as compression applies.

examples.mini_scenario: The window overflows; ContextOverflowCompress trims history to the target token count and the loop resumes without losing the task.
examples.pitfall: Preserve the task and recent tool results when compressing; over-aggressive trimming drops the goal itself.

examples.title: Reload credentials on auth failure
examples.intent: Rebuild the client with a fresh key after a 401/403.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The ReloadCredentials directive picks a new key via CredentialReload and rebuilds the client, letting the same call succeed on retry.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the credential node to trigger a manual key reload from keyring/env.
touch_interaction.visual: A key icon spins then locks green when a working credential is found, red if none available.

examples.mini_scenario: A 401 classifies as AuthError; find_available_key locates an alternate endpoint key and the rebuilt client retries successfully.
examples.pitfall: Bound reload attempts; endlessly rotating through exhausted keys turns auth recovery into a loop.

examples.title: Back off on rate limits
examples.intent: Wait before retrying a 429 so the endpoint recovers.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RateLimitBackoff inserts an increasing delay before the retry, spacing out attempts within a max_attempts budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the retry edge to see the backoff delay and remaining attempts.
touch_interaction.visual: A countdown ring shows the wait; the attempt counter ticks toward max_attempts.

examples.mini_scenario: A 429 classifies as RateLimited; RateLimitBackoff waits delay_ms then retries, doubling on repeated hits until max_attempts.
examples.pitfall: Honor Retry-After when present; a fixed backoff can still hammer an endpoint that asked for a longer wait.

examples.title: Checkpoint state before a risky act
examples.intent: Capture a restorable StateCheckpoint before a step that might fail.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: StateManager.checkpoint records the current state so the loop can roll back instead of losing progress on failure.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the state node to drop a checkpoint pin on the loop timeline.
touch_interaction.visual: A pin marker lands on the timeline with a description label and timestamp.

examples.mini_scenario: Before a multi-file edit, StateManager.checkpoint snapshots the state so a partial failure can be reverted.
examples.pitfall: Include the components that will change; a checkpoint missing the mutated component cannot fully restore it.

examples.title: Restore from the latest checkpoint
examples.intent: Revert to a known-good state after a failed step.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: StateManager.restore returns a StateCheckpoint the loop reloads, transitioning from ErrorRecovery back to a consistent Executing state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a checkpoint pin to restore the loop to that snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: The timeline rewinds visually to the pin; downstream state cards reset to the snapshot values.

examples.mini_scenario: A migration corrupts state; StateManager.latest returns the pre-migration checkpoint and the loop restores it.
examples.pitfall: Restore is only as good as the snapshot; restoring a checkpoint taken after the corruption reloads the bad state.

examples.title: Predict health before it fails
examples.intent: Forecast a component sliding toward failure so the loop acts early.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: HealthPredictor.predict emits a HealthPrediction with a PredictedHealth and time_until_issue, letting control intervene before a hard failure.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread the predictor node to see per-component health trajectories.
touch_interaction.visual: Each component shows a trend line; a downward slope tints toward FailureImminent red.

examples.mini_scenario: Latency trends worsen; predict returns Degrading with a time_until_issue, so the loop preemptively switches to a fallback.
examples.pitfall: Act on AtRisk/Degrading, not only FailureImminent; waiting for imminent leaves no lead time to recover.

examples.title: Attach a recommended action to a prediction
examples.intent: Pair each forecast with the action that would head off the failure.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: HealthPrediction.recommended_action gives control a ready RecoveryAction so the perceive->act path is short.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a prediction card to reveal its recommended RecoveryAction button.
touch_interaction.visual: The card shows the predicted status plus an actionable button tinted by urgency.

examples.mini_scenario: A FailureImminent prediction for the GPU recommends a restart action, which the operator triggers with one tap.
examples.pitfall: A recommendation is a hint, not a mandate; auto-executing a heavy action on a low-confidence prediction can thrash.

examples.title: Track prediction accuracy
examples.intent: Learn whether past predictions were right to trust future ones.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: record_outcome updates accuracy, so the loop can weight or ignore predictions from a poorly-calibrated predictor.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the predictor to see its running accuracy score.
touch_interaction.visual: An accuracy dial fills green as correct predictions accumulate, red as it mispredicts.

examples.mini_scenario: A predicted failure never materializes; record_outcome(false) lowers accuracy and future predictions are trusted less.
examples.pitfall: Feed real outcomes back consistently; an unlabeled predictor's accuracy is meaningless and misleading.

examples.title: Detect a deadlock with no progress
examples.intent: Notice when the loop is waiting without making progress.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DeadlockDetector.observe flags a Deadlock FailureKind after a threshold of waiting-without-progress, forcing a recovery transition.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the deadlock detector to see the current no-progress count against its threshold.
touch_interaction.visual: A stall meter fills; crossing the threshold flashes a Deadlock badge on the loop.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop waits repeatedly with no progress; observe crosses the threshold and returns Deadlock so recovery can break it.
examples.pitfall: Reset the counter on genuine progress; forgetting to reset accumulates false deadlock signals.

examples.title: Fall back to a local endpoint
examples.intent: Switch to a local model when the primary endpoint is unreachable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LocalEndpointFallback resolves an LlmUnreachable by redirecting the loop to a local endpoint so work continues degraded.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the endpoint selector from Remote to Local to enable the fallback.
touch_interaction.visual: The endpoint node swaps its cloud icon for a local-machine icon and turns amber to signal degraded mode.

examples.mini_scenario: The remote endpoint refuses connections; LocalEndpointFallback (opt-in) reroutes to the local model and the loop keeps running.
examples.pitfall: Fallback must be opt-in and capability-aware; silently downgrading to a weaker local model can degrade output quality.

examples.title: Bound retries with the executor
examples.intent: Cap how many times a pattern is retried before giving up.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RecoveryExecutor tracks retry_attempt_count per pattern and stops when exhausted, protecting the loop's overall budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch a recovering node to see its attempt count against the retry cap.
touch_interaction.visual: A segmented retry gauge fills per attempt; the last segment turns red at the cap.

examples.mini_scenario: A pattern hits its retry cap; the executor stops retrying and lets the loop transition to Failed rather than spinning.
examples.pitfall: Reset retry state after success with reset_retry_state; a stale count can prematurely exhaust a fresh failure.

examples.title: Record recovery success rates
examples.intent: Feed recovery results back so strategy selection improves.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: record_recovery marks a strategy success/failure, updating success_rate so recommend_recovery favors what actually works.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a completed recovery card into the learner to log its outcome.
touch_interaction.visual: The card animates into the learner and the associated strategy's success ring updates.

examples.mini_scenario: A retry strategy succeeds; record_recovery logs the win and raises that strategy's rank for the pattern.
examples.pitfall: Attribute the outcome to the strategy that actually ran, not the recommended one, if they diverged.

examples.title: Handle disk-full failures distinctly
examples.intent: Route ENOSPC to a cleanup recovery rather than a blind retry.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: classify maps a disk-full message to DiskFull, letting the RecoveryTree pick a space-reclaiming path instead of retrying the doomed write.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a DiskFull failure to see its dedicated recovery path.
touch_interaction.visual: The failure badge shows a disk icon; its recovery edge routes to a cleanup node, not retry.

examples.mini_scenario: A write fails with ENOSPC; classify returns DiskFull so recovery reclaims space before re-attempting the write.
examples.pitfall: Do not retry DiskFull without freeing space; an immediate retry just reproduces the same ENOSPC.

examples.title: Register custom resolvers on the tree
examples.intent: Add new FailureKind-to-Resolution mappings without changing the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RecoveryTree.register wires a resolver for a FailureKind, extending the ErrorRecovery branch's coverage as new failure modes appear.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag a resolver chip onto a FailureKind slot in the recovery tree to bind it.
touch_interaction.visual: The slot fills with the resolver's icon; unbound kinds show a dashed placeholder.

examples.mini_scenario: A new provider-specific error kind is added; register binds a custom resolver so resolve dispatches it correctly.
examples.pitfall: Cover the FailureKinds you care about; an unregistered kind falls through to Unknown with generic handling.

examples.title: Compose the ErrorRecovery branch end to end
examples.intent: Wire learning, classification, recovery, and prediction into one recovery subsystem.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Chains ErrorLearner (record+recommend) -> RecoveryTree (classify+directive) -> RecoveryExecutor (bounded retry) -> StateManager (rollback), with HealthPredictor pre-empting failures.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch to collapse the self-healing sub-nodes into one recovery node on the loop's ErrorRecovery edge.
touch_interaction.visual: Collapsed it shows a healing-cross badge with the active strategy; spread reveals the learner, tree, executor, state, and predictor pipeline.

examples.mini_scenario: An error is recorded and classified, the tree emits a CompressContext directive within the retry budget, and on repeated failure StateManager restores the last checkpoint.
examples.pitfall: Keep learning and acting in order: classify before dispatching, checkpoint before risky recovery, and feed outcomes back so the system actually learns.
